provenance: MEASURED on the G1A (the development machine), not synthetic and not a Claude Code capture. Every value here was read back from a live WSL2 Ubuntu distro and from this repo's own resolution code executed by a real Linux Node inside it. It sits in a synthetic- directory because the directory's other file is hand-made; this one is not - see README.md. One class of value is REDACTED rather than verbatim: see the redaction block below, and do not read a <redacted-user> token as a measurement.
howMeasured: src/model/pathmatrix.probe.ts bundled with esbuild (esm, platform=node) and run as: wsl.exe -- <linuxNode> <bundle> --agent-deck-path-probe fixtures/synthetic-path-matrix/slug-cases.json. src/model/pathmatrix.test.ts re-runs exactly that and refuses to disagree with this file.

redaction.destroyed: The WSL-side account name. Every Linux-side home path is stored as the literal token /home/<redacted-user>, and the UNC spelling of it as \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\<redacted-user> - neither token is a path, and neither ever existed on any machine.
redaction.kept: Everything the measurement is about: that $HOME is a posix absolute path under /home, that the Linux projects root is $HOME/.claude/projects joined with '/', that wslpath -w maps a Linux path to \\wsl.localhost\<distro>\<the same path, backslashed>, the distro and kernel identifiers that date the measurement, and both Windows spellings of the workspace. Also kept: sha256 digests of the two redacted strings, so a re-run can still prove it is describing THIS machine and not a different one.
redaction.whyNotTheWindowsSide: The Windows-side account name stays verbatim here and in slug-cases.json because it is irreducible: Claude Code itself wrote the directory name c--Users-dev-projects-agent-deck under fixtures/cc-2.1.234/projects, that directory is the only cc-capture witness in the matrix, and redacting the path it decodes from would destroy the witness while removing nothing from the repo. The WSL side has the opposite property: claudeDirectoryPresent is false, no capture exists on that side of the boundary, and every posix/wslMount row is witness=encoding-rule, so no evidence depends on the account name.
redaction.notASecret: These digests are stability pins, not protection. A short POSIX account name is low-entropy and a sha256 of it is trivially reversible from a username list; the name is in any case already present in the Windows paths this repo keeps deliberately. What the redaction buys is category containment: the POSIX-home and UNC-wsl shapes no longer appear here with an account name in them, so a later edit cannot silently reintroduce a category that a Windows-path privacy sweep does not look for. The patterns are in the privacy section of README.md and are enforced by a test.
redaction.sha256Of: the exact byte string shown, with no trailing newline

wsl.claudeDirectoryNote: No Claude Code has ever run inside this distro: $HOME/.claude does not exist, and the `claude` on the WSL PATH is the Windows npm shim reached through /mnt/c interop, not a Linux install. Consequence: no posix slug in slug-cases.json is witnessed from CC itself.
wsl.linuxNodeNote: Unpacked from the official tarball for this leg; the distro ships no Node. Not part of any checkout, which is why the WSL leg announces a skip when it cannot find one. Recorded in $HOME-relative form for the same reason the home path is redacted; the test resolves it with `command -v`, which expands $HOME inside the distro.

wslpath.neutralLinuxPathNote: MEASURED 2026-08-20: `wslpath -w /home/probe/agent-deck`. /home/probe does not exist in the distro - /home holds exactly one account - and wslpath -w never stats the path, so this pair pins the same UNC translation rule the real home did while carrying no account name. It is the path slug-cases.json's unc-wsl-localhost row decodes from.

slugs.note: One physical directory, two spellings, two slugs. They are not case variants: lowercasing both leaves them different. Agent Deck never translates between the two - see the WSL boundary note in src/model/correlate.ts.
